interactions.title: Azogar tells the tale of the cloak
lines: DM: But as the night—as the time passes midnight, the fires died down and one of the old orcs, the loremaster Azogar stands up, and to the beat of the drums behind him he begins to chant the tale of the Cloak of the Rainbow.

DM: He tells—and this is the first time you've heard the whole story told in full—he tells of the first days of the people of the Rainbow, before there was a cloak, of Ilios the Bright, who fell through the world when he was just an infant, not yet chained to Thark's will, and grew strong in the fey realm of Amberglow under a sunset sky free of Thark's influence.

DM: How Ilios, the tale continues, had a fey energy that could not be contained. His eyes shone with moonlight, and his swords flashed silver, and he began to raid across the foothills of the sentinels, where small, disorganized orcs hid in family groups and tribes from the Drankorian patrols. And the people of the Rainbow grew in secret, protected by the Cloudspinner, as Ilios stole through the world, taking babies as they were born back to Amberglow with him.

DM: And then Azogar speaks of the blackness that tore out the sun, the rift through which darkness leaked, the invasion of Amberglow by a far distant evil, something of no world. And Ilios leapt through this blackness and severed the cords that held this rift open, trapping himself to an unknown fate, but saving Amberglow.

DM: And in exchange the Cloudspinner wove the cloak, each thread plucked from the immortal sunsets of Amberglow, each thread grasping the essence of the long pause of the splitting of the planes that created the Feywild, and wrapping that energy of pulling, separating into a cloak that cut the wearer from the divine.
DM: And then the story tells of the days in the world when the people of the rainbow ventured forth: quiet days, living the quiet lives of fields and flowers.

DM: And then Azogar turns grim and speaks the tale of Cha'mutte and Apollyon. Cha'mutte traveling among the Orcs, teaching them, telling telling them of the fate he sought for for all the orcs: everybody to be like the people of the rainbow, telling Apollyon of this dream of the cloak. And then the war and betrayal and loss, as Apollyon turned on the orcs, stole the cloak, and then Cha'mutte's revenge. But it was too late. The cloak was lost, the people scattered to the winds, hiding in small groups across the world, hiding from Thark as best they could until after the great war.

DM: The triumph of Uzgash! The cloak found. Xurkhaz, the land of the rising sun, the beacon of hope for Orcs across the world restored to its glory by the hero, Uzgash. He recovered the cloak from a hidden Dunmari fortress.

DM: And then Azogar adds to the story, the heroism of the dwarf Riswynn pacing the city, day after day after day after day. Never before the orcs of of the people of the Rainbow believed that the power of the divine could be used for good.
DM: And yet it saved them.

DM: And then Lord Boulder, the hero of the battle for Uzgukhar. The Orc, standing and watching from the city—the ruined city— as out of nowhere, a giant siege engine that had destroyed their walls was shattered to pieces. One fell blow.

DM: And the tale ends on that note of triumph as Lubash stands there, the cloak shining bright behind him. The Orcs cheer, and there are many thanks and songs of praise late into the night. Songs, songs of gratitude for Riswynn, but also mostly for Riswynn.
